podcast.title: 2005 Warner Music Group Dispute
podcast.body: In spring 2005, Warner, the band's record label, requested they perform at the New York Stock Exchange to celebrate its IPO following a significant financial restructuring that included $250 million in cuts. Lincoln Park was incensed by the cuts, believing they would hinder the label's ability to promote their music and other artists, and publicly refused to play, highlighting that they received no share from the IPO despite having sold 57 million records with just two albums. "Lincoln Park, though, was pissed at this one."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Favorable Contract Renegotiation (2005)
podcast.body: After a public dispute with Warner Music Group, Lincoln Park secured a $15 million advance for their next album, "Minutes to Midnight," and an option for up to five additional albums with an exceptionally high royalty rate of 20%. Warner had little choice but to agree, given their new presence in financial markets and the risk of losing "the biggest rock band in the world at the time." "Lincoln Park had a $15 million advance for the next album which was Minutes to Midnight. They were also given an option for up to 5 more albums with a royalty rate of 20%, which is a pretty insanely high rate."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Carpool Karaoke Appearance (2017)
podcast.body: On July 14, 2017, the band filmed an episode of "Carpool Karaoke" with James Corden. Footage from the event showed Chester Bennington appearing happy and healthy just days before his death. "On July 14, 2017, the band shot an episode of Carpool Karaoke with James Corden. That seemed to be loads of fun."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Chester Bennington Tribute Concert (2017)
podcast.body: On October 27, 2017, a three-hour tribute concert for Chester Bennington was held at the Hollywood Bowl. The event featured friends from Blink 182, System of a Down, Korn, and Avenged Sevenfold, and was streamed live, reaching millions of viewers as Linkin Park paid tribute to their fallen bandmate. "On October 27th, 2017, there was a three hour tribute to Chester featuring his friends from Blink 182, system of a downed corn, a bench, seven fold and more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Career Success & Control
podcast.body: By 2011, approximately 10 years after forming, Lincoln Park had sold over 80 million albums and amassed millions of fans globally. They exercised firm control over their career, dictating a schedule of releasing a new album every 18 months, rather than their record label. "In the 10 years since the band was formed, they'd sold over 80 million albums."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Embraced Modern Electronic Drums
podcast.body: Rob Borden of Lincoln Park is one of the contemporary drummers who has adopted modern electronic drums. These instruments are utilized to trigger sounds, tones, patterns, and samples, demonstrating their versatility in modern music production and performance. "Today's electronic drums have been embraced by players such as Danny Carey, Neil Peart, Will Champion of Coldplay, Rob Borden of Lincoln Park, and many, many others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of the Modern Drum Kit

podcast.title: Initial Record Label Rejections
podcast.body: Their demos were turned down by record labels almost 50 times before they were signed at the end of 1999, which reflected the music industry's belief that new metal was "over" at that time. "And to think that their demos were turned down by record labels almost 50 times before they were signed at the end of 1999, that's how much the industry believed that new metal was over."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: LP Recharge Online Game
podcast.body: Chester Bennington was involved in the creation of "LP Recharge," an online action game based on the band itself. The game was launched through Facebook, demonstrating the band's engagement with new digital platforms. "He was also involved in the creation of LP Recharge, which was an online action game based on the band and launched through Facebook."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Members' Side Projects
podcast.body: The band members, all in their 30s by 2011, found time to pursue various side projects, encompassing both musical and non-musical endeavors. These included remix albums, contributions to soundtracks, and even movies, with DJ Johan notably starting to direct films. "Plus, they had time to indulge in all kinds of side projects, some musical, some not, like remix album, soundtracks, even movies, DJ Johan had started to direct films."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Most Successful New Metal Descendant
podcast.body: Linkin Park is considered the most successful of all the bands to descend from the new metal era, having created a superior and more cohesive hybrid of alternative rock and rap. "No other band ever created a better and more cohesive hybrid of alternative rock and rap than these guys."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: New Metal Era Foundation
podcast.body: Linkin Park's existence and massive success (over 100 million records sold) would not have been possible had they not been "bored in the new metal era of the late 90s." "Lincoln Park would not have existed or sold 100 million records had they not been bored in the new metal era of the late 90s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: One More Light Fund Establishment
podcast.body: In memory of Chester Bennington, Linkin Park established the "One More Light Fund," an organization dedicated to offering help and support to individuals grappling with mental health issues. "And in Chester's memory, Lincoln Park has the one more light fund, an organization that offers help to those who need it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-1990s Release
podcast.body: Although born in the new metal era of the late 90s, the specific song mentioned came out in 2000, not the 90s. "Now to be very fair, that song came out in 2000 and not in the 90s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Public Contract Negotiation
podcast.body: The band issued a press release criticizing Warner Music Group for an expected $1.4 billion windfall from their IPO, with only $7 million going to company operations and nothing to artists, while Warner fired back accusing the band's management of using "fictitious numbers" and "inflammatory threats" as a negotiating tactic. This public dispute lasted for months, drawing significant media attention. "This very public fight went on for months before an agreement was reached."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Record Industry Evolution & Sales Decline
podcast.body: Over their career, the band witnessed a drastic shift in the record industry; their first album sold 30 million copies, but by their sixth album in 2014, worldwide sales barely reached a million. This decline in physical sales was attributed to streaming taking over, yet the band sustained itself through touring and a deep catalog. "By the time the numbers started coming in for their sixth album in 2014, World Wide Sales barely added up to a million."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sophisticated Online & Social Media Strategy
podcast.body: Lincoln Park developed an exceptionally smart and effective online and social media organization, recognized for its modern 21st-century approach to engaging and maintaining their fanbase. The band members were deeply involved, constantly interacting, providing special content, and releasing music directly to fans. "I have never seen an organization smarter than the one behind Lincoln Park."

xref.title: Extended Hiatus (2004-2007)
xref.body: Following intense touring and recording through 2004, Linkin Park took an almost four-year break from releasing proper studio albums. During this hiatus, individual band members pursued various side projects and collaborations to maintain their creative output. "by the end of 2004 Lincoln Park needed a break. So they disappeared for almost four solid years."

xref.title: Chester Bennington's Cell Phone Hacked (Late March 2006)
xref.body: The band's cyberstalking crisis began in late March 2006 when Linkin Park vocalist Chester Bennington had his cell phone hacked. This incident occurred during an earlier technological era, predating the widespread use of iPhones and modern cybersecurity features like two-factor authentication, facial recognition, and strong password reminders. "In late March of that year, Lincoln Park vocalist Chester Bennington had his cell phone hacked."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Uncharted "Sneak Peak" - Episode 7: The Linkin Park Cyberstalker

xref.title: Stalker Impersonates Talinda to Security (Spring 2006)
xref.body: Bruce Thompson, Linkin Park's head of security at the time, received an email purporting to be from Talinda, inquiring about Chester's ex-wife Samantha's email address and mentioning "Strange emails from fansources have been received" with "a lot of information." Bruce initially believed Talinda sent the message, but it was later revealed to be from the mystery cyberstalker. "Back then, Lincoln Park had a head of security, his name was Bruce Thompson, and he got an email that was supposed to be from Talinda."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Commercial Success by 2009
xref.body: By the end of 2009, after releasing just three studio albums, Linkin Park had sold an impressive 80 million albums, establishing them as "the most successful new rock band to emerge in the 21st century." "Lincoln Park was on its way to selling 80 million albums, making them the most successful new rock band to emerge in the 21st century."

xref.title: Chester Bennington Joins (2013)
xref.body: In May 2013, after firing Scott Weiland, the band announced that Chester Bennington of Linkin Park would join as a full-time member. This arrangement lasted about 18 months, during which they toured extensively and released one 5-track EP. "In May of that year, they announced that Chester Bennington of Lincoln Park was the new guy and as a full-time member too."

xref.title: Accident-Proneness and Tour Interruptions
xref.body: Chester experienced a series of physical misfortunes, including breaking a wrist during a Melbourne show in 2007, falling ill while touring Asia in 2011 (causing five Linkin Park show cancellations), sustaining a shoulder injury requiring immediate surgery in 2011, and damaging his ankle playing basketball in 2015, which also necessitated surgery and further show cancellations. "he was rather accident prone. In 2007, he broke a wrist during a show in Melbourne. In 2011, he got sick while touring Asia, which affected five Lincoln Park shows. And then he injured his shoulder, which required immediate surgery."

xref.title: Contribution to Linkin Park's Name
xref.body: Chester Bennington was credited with suggesting the name "Linkin Park" after driving past a real Lincoln Park in Santa Monica. The band also appreciated the national appeal of a name associated with Abraham Lincoln. "But it was Chester who came up with the name that stuck. He was driving past a real Lincoln Park in Santa Monica."

xref.body: Chester initiated his side project, initially named Snow White Tan and later Dead by Sunrise, specifically to accommodate songs he had written that "weren't right for Lincoln Park," collaborating with friends from the bands Julian K and Orgy. "The group began because Chester had written some songs that really weren't right for Lincoln Park."

xref.title: Date of Death and Cause
xref.body: Chester Bennington, the vocalist for Linkin Park, was confirmed dead by his own hand on Thursday, July 20, 2017. His death came as a shock and was widely considered unexpected, even among a series of other musician deaths around that time. "Chester Bennington, vocalist with Lincoln Park, was not only dead, but dead by his own hand."

xref.title: Early Phoenix Bands
xref.body: Before moving to Los Angeles to audition for Hybrid Theory (which became Linkin Park), Chester Bennington was active in the Phoenix music scene. Around age 17 in 1993, he sang in a band with his friend Sean, initially "Sean Dattel and his friends?" and then co-formed Gray Daze, which existed from late 1993 through 1998. "We now turn our attention to the parts that came together to form Lincoln Park, specifically what Chester Bennington was up to in Phoenix before he was invited to move to LA to sing for this new group."

xref.title: Emergence from New Metal
xref.body: Linkin Park was one of the few groups to emerge from the late 1990s' "new metal" scene bigger and stronger, distinguishing themselves with a pop sensibility that made their angry and powerful music highly catchy. "Lincoln Park is pretty much the only group to emerge from the whole new metal thing of the late 90s bigger and stronger."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Emerging New Metal Offshoot
xref.body: Linkin Park was introduced as a "new band out of LA" that, while not purely new metal, exhibited some of the genre's sonic trappings, suggesting their emergence as part of the broader new metal wave. "Crazy town, popper roach, disturbed, and this new band out of LA called Lincoln Park."

xref.title: Extended Hiatus After Chester Bennington's Death
xref.body: Following the death of lead singer Chester Bennington in July 2017, Linkin Park entered a prolonged period of inactivity as the remaining members grappled with the loss and adjusted to the tragedy. The band was absent from the music scene for a considerable time, with their eventual return in late 2024 accompanied by lineup changes. "Lincoln Park was absent from the scene for a long, long time after Chester's death as everybody tried to adjust."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Extensive Documentation
xref.body: Linkin Park's journey and story are exceptionally well-documented by various entities, including the band members themselves, their management company, their record label, and their dedicated fanbase. "Lincoln Park is a very 21st century band and the sense that their story is so very well documented by themselves, their management company, their label, and their fans."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Genre Evolution with Minutes to Midnight
xref.body: With "Minutes to Midnight," Linkin Park made a deliberate choice to shift their sound away from "pure new metal" into "a different sort of headspace." This change was partly evidenced by Mike Shinoda's increased singing roles and reduced rapping, appearing on only two of the album's 12 songs. "Lincoln Park made a conscious decision to move away from pure new metal into a different sort of headspace."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Initial Label Disdain for Sound
xref.body: Warner Brothers Records executives, including reportedly the label president, initially struggled to understand and even disliked Linkin Park's sound, characterized by "screaming and rapping." There was even internal debate about whether to release their debut record at all. "Warner did not know what to do with Lincoln Park and some, including apparently the president of the label just hated their sound."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Live 8 Performance - Philadelphia
xref.body: Coldplay was one of the many artists and celebrities who appeared at the Live 8 global telecast benefit concert on July 2nd, 2005. "You too, audio, life, green day, Roxy music, James Brown, Nelson Mandela, Bill Gates, Brad Pitt, David Beckham, Ricky Gervais, Coldplay, Madonna, REM, the killer, Sting, the cure, Lincoln Park, Sarah McLaughlin, Will Smith, and Durand Durand, and a whole bunch of others."

xref.title: Live Music Mention
xref.body: Linkin Park was mentioned in the context of playing live music. No specific details about recordings, albums, or concerts were provided beyond the name. "How about this from Lincoln Park?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Weird History of Concert Tickets Part 1

xref.title: Most Pirated Rock Artist
xref.body: Linkin Park was identified as the most pirated rock act of the 2000s, with their music, particularly from the *Hybrid Theory* album, being widely shared illegally. "No one had their music pirated more apparently than Lincoln Park."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 10: (10-1)

xref.title: Name Change from Hybrid Theory
xref.body: The band changed its name to "Linkin Park" from "Hybrid Theory" after being inspired by an actual park of the same name in Santa Monica that they drove by daily. They believed it to be a universally recognizable name, as many American towns reportedly have a Lincoln Park. "Hybrid Theory became the deliberately misspelled Lincoln Park."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: New Metal Offshoot
xref.body: Papa Roach was listed among "offshoot" groups that integrated some of the sonic elements of new metal into their music, even if they weren't considered pure new metal bands themselves. "Crazy town, popper roach, disturbed, and this new band out of LA called Lincoln Park."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: New Metal Offshoot
xref.body: Disturbed was mentioned as a band that, though not strictly pure new metal, shared some of the sonic characteristics and stylistic traits of the genre during its peak popularity. "Crazy town, popper roach, disturbed, and this new band out of LA called Lincoln Park."

xref.title: North American Tour & Gray Days Reunion Plans
xref.body: Following the Europe tour, a short break was planned before a 29-date North American tour in support of the number one album "One More Light." Around this time, Chester was also discussing a potential reunion with Gray Days, his pre-Linkin Park band from Arizona. "Chester was talking about a reunion with Gray Days, a band from his pre-Lincoln Park days in Arizona."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Online Savvy from Piracy
xref.body: The challenge of widespread piracy compelled Linkin Park to develop one of the most sophisticated online presences among bands. This experience made them highly adept at managing piracy issues and engaging with their fanbase digitally. "piracy forced Lincoln Park to become one of the most savvy bands in the world when it came to online presence."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 10: (10-1)

xref.title: Online Security History
xref.body: While Linkin Park's management later became very conscious of security, the band's online presence was not always as secure as it is in the present day. This historical lack of comprehensive security contributed to significant vulnerabilities. "But the online world of Lincoln Park wasn't always as secure as it is today."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Uncharted "Sneak Peak" - Episode 7: The Linkin Park Cyberstalker

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Pioneering Online Fan Club
xref.body: Linkin Park established a high-level fan club and street team called "Linkin Park Underground," which focused on serving fans online. This dedication to online fan engagement was a novel approach for bands at the time. "They created a high-level fan club slash street team called Lincoln Park Underground that strove to serve the fans online, something that few bands were doing at the time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Producer for Minutes to Midnight
xref.body: Rick Rubin served as the producer for Linkin Park's third studio album, Minutes to Midnight, a project that spanned approximately 18 months of work. "Lincoln Park spent about 18 months working on their third album, this time with producer Rick Rubin."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Project Revolution CD Initiative
xref.body: During the Project Revolution tour in 2007-2008, Linkin Park implemented an innovative merchandise strategy: they sold blank CDs at their merch booths for $11, each containing a download code that allowed fans to download and burn that specific Linkin Park show for personal use. "Each came with a download code that allowed any fan to download and burn that particular Lincoln Park show for their personal use."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Radio Friendly Sound
xref.body: Linkin Park was recognized for its broad appeal and "super radio friendly" sound, which distinguished them within the New Metal genre, even as the genre itself was largely declining. "Lincoln Park was super radio friendly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Twilight Soundtracks Contribution
xref.body: Paramore contributed to the various *Twilight* soundtracks that accompanied the film series. These soundtracks featured a nice selection of tunes, mostly album cuts and outtakes, from a range of artists spanning different genres. "The Paramore, Lincoln Park, Collective Soul, Death Cab for Cutie, Tom York, the Killers, Editors, Metric, Block Keys, Dead Weather, Beck, Vampire Weekend, Florence in the Machine."

xref.title: Upcoming Tour and Reunion Plans
xref.body: At the time of his death, Chester Bennington was preparing for a 29-date Linkin Park tour and had committed to a reunion with his former band, Grey Daze, after the tour concluded. He appeared happy, secure, and in excellent physical condition. "A 29-date Lincoln Park tour was about to start, and once that was over, he'd committed to joining Gray Days, the band he was in before Lincoln Park, for a reunion."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

"Here's a short list of artists who say they were inspired and influenced by Skinny Puppy, Ministry, Nine-inch Nails, Maryland Manson, the Prodigy, Ramstein, Filter, Corn, Lincoln Park, Evan Essence."
